title: Human Problem Solving
authors: Allen Newell, Herbert A. Simon
problem: Modeling human cognition and problem solving via explicit memory structures and production systems.
memory_representation: Production rules, working memory elements, associative long-term memory structures.
memory_storage: Symbolic production system state and working memory buffer.
memory_write: Rule activation and working memory element insertion.
memory_update: Working memory displacement and state replacement.
memory_retrieval: Pattern matching over working memory against production preconditions.
memory_persistence: Persistent long-term rule base with transient working memory.
branching: Search trees in problem spaces (heuristic search).
contradiction_handling: Conflict resolution strategies (specificity, recency).
context_budget: Working memory capacity limits (7 +/- 2 chunks).
evaluation: Empirical human protocol analysis.
major_findings: Cognitive problem solving relies on small working memory interacting with large associative long-term store.
limitations: Symbolic brittleness; manual engineering of rules.
relevance_to_manigit: Establishes foundational distinction between bounded working memory (context) and persistent long-term storage.

title: On the Logic of Theory Change: Partial Meet Contraction and Revision Functions
authors: Carlos E. Alchourron, Peter Gardenfors, David Makinson
problem: Formalizing logical constraints on revising beliefs in the face of contradictory new information.
memory_representation: Propositional belief sets and deductively closed theories.
memory_write: Expansion operator (+).
memory_update: Revision (*) and contraction (-) operations.
memory_retrieval: Logical entailment.
contradiction_handling: AGM revision postulates: Success, Consistency, Minimal Change.
historical_reconstruction: None (retracts old beliefs to preserve consistency).
context_budget: None
evaluation: Mathematical theorem proving.
major_findings: Defined mathematical postulates for minimal information loss during contradictory belief updates.
limitations: Intractable for large propositional spaces; assumes full logical omniscience.
relevance_to_manigit: Direct theoretical foundation for ManiGit contradiction handling, supersession, and non-destructive historical preservation.

title: Neural Turing Machines
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Ivo Danihelka
problem: Enabling neural networks to read and write external working memory matrices using differentiable addressing.
memory_representation: Dense real-valued memory matrix M of size N x W.
memory_write: Differentiable erase and add vectors gated by write heads.
memory_update: Continuous element-wise matrix modification.
memory_retrieval: Content-based and location-based differentiable read heads.
contradiction_handling: Continuous overwriting via erase vector.
context_budget: Fixed memory matrix dimensions (N x W).
evaluation: Algorithmic synthetic tasks (copy, repeat copy, associative recall).
major_findings: Neural networks can learn algorithmic memory management using differentiable read/write addressing.
limitations: Difficult optimization; memory capacity does not scale cleanly to long open-domain text.
relevance_to_manigit: Precedent for explicit externalized memory addressing distinct from model weights.

title: Memory Networks
authors: Jason Weston, Sumit Chopra, Antoine Bordes
problem: Traditional RNNs cannot explicitly store and recall long-term facts for multi-turn reasoning.
memory_representation: Array of continuous memory slots storing sentence representations.
memory_write: Appending incoming sentence vectors to indexed slots.
memory_update: Append-only during dialogue.
memory_retrieval: Dot-product scoring between query and memory slots followed by output mapping.
memory_persistence: In-memory data structure for task duration.
provenance: Direct memory slot index linkage to source sentence.
contradiction_handling: None (retrieves top matches regardless of conflict).
context_budget: Bounded number of memory slots.
evaluation: Synthetic bAbI Q&A tasks and QA benchmarks.
major_findings: Explicit memory slot addressing enables multi-hop reasoning that standard sequence models fail.
limitations: Fixed capacity; no dynamic summarization or contradiction resolution.
relevance_to_manigit: Direct predecessor to slot-based fact retrieval; demonstrates need for structured memory over hidden states.

title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Malcolm Reynolds, et al.
problem: Neural Turing Machines struggled with free memory allocation, temporal ordering, and graph traversal.
memory_representation: Dense memory matrix with temporal link matrix and memory usage vectors.
memory_write: Dynamic memory allocation using usage vectors and temporal links.
memory_update: Dynamic deallocation and write-over of freed locations.
memory_retrieval: Content-based similarity and temporal directional traversal (forward/backward).
versioning: Temporal link matrix tracks write order.
contradiction_handling: Overwriting unallocated or freed memory slots.
context_budget: Fixed memory matrix size.
evaluation: Graph traversal, shortest path, family trees, London Underground transit.
major_findings: Dynamic memory allocation and temporal tracking allow neural networks to solve complex graph reasoning.
limitations: Extremely computationally heavy; hard to scale to symbolic natural language.
relevance_to_manigit: Pioneered temporal linking of memory writes; ManiGit implements temporal provenance symbolically via commit DAGs.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, et al.
problem: Sequential recurrent computation bottlenecked long-range dependency modeling and parallelization.
memory_representation: Token embeddings with multi-head self-attention activations.
memory_storage: Transient key-value (KV) attention cache during generation.
memory_write: Appending token representations to KV cache.
memory_update: Append-only during autoregressive rollout.
memory_retrieval: Soft dot-product attention over all prefix tokens.
contradiction_handling: None (processes conflicting tokens simultaneously).
historical_reconstruction: Full context available up to context limit L.
context_budget: Hard sequence length limit L (quadratic complexity in early implementations).
evaluation: WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation.
major_findings: Attention alone provides powerful context routing without recurrence.
limitations: Context is ephemeral and bounded; memory does not persist across independent inference calls.
relevance_to_manigit: Defines the fundamental context window abstraction that ManiGit compiles into under token budgets.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
authors: Kelvin Guu, Kenton Lee, Zora Tung, Panupong Pasupat, Ming-Wei Chang
problem: Parametric language models store factual knowledge in weights, leading to hallucinations and high retraining costs.
memory_representation: Text passages indexed via dense neural embeddings.
memory_storage: MIPS (Maximum Inner Product Search) external vector index.
memory_write: Pre-computing passage embeddings using neural encoder.
memory_update: Re-indexing vector embeddings periodically.
memory_retrieval: Differentiable dense retrieval over passage embeddings.
contradiction_handling: None (retrieves passages with high inner product).
context_budget: Top-k passages injected into model context.
evaluation: Open-domain QA benchmarks (Natural Questions, WebQuestions, CuratedTREC).
major_findings: End-to-end differentiable retrieval pre-training significantly improves factual open-domain question answering.
limitations: Static document store; no multi-turn conversational agent interaction or state evolution.
relevance_to_manigit: Predecessor to modern retrieval augmentation; demonstrates offloading memory from parameters to external stores.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandara Piktus, et al.
problem: General-purpose pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models cannot update world knowledge or provide citations.
memory_representation: Dense passage vectors paired with Wikipedia text passages.
memory_storage: DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) FAISS vector index.
memory_write: Offline passage embedding and indexing.
memory_update: External index replacement.
memory_retrieval: Dense similarity search (RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence models).
contradiction_handling: None (marginalizes over retrieved passages).
context_budget: Top-k passages (fixed token budget).
evaluation: Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, Jeopardy, FEVER.
major_findings: Combining parametric generator with non-parametric retrieval yields state-of-the-art factual generation and verifiable sources.
limitations: Designed for static reference text, not dynamic agent conversation state; lacks conflict resolution.
relevance_to_manigit: ManiGit directly evaluates against RAG as a baseline, showing RAG fails on temporal supersession.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
authors: Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder, et al.
problem: Task-specific fine-tuning requires large labeled datasets for every downstream application.
memory_representation: In-context prompt demonstrations and token sequence.
memory_write: Prompt formulation.
memory_update: Prompt rewriting.
memory_retrieval: Autoregressive attention across in-context examples.
contradiction_handling: In-context recency bias.
context_budget: Hard limit: 2,048 tokens.
evaluation: Broad NLP benchmark suite (SuperGLUE, TriviaQA, arithmetic, translation).
major_findings: Scaling autoregressive models enables few-shot in-context learning without gradient updates.
limitations: Context window acts as bottleneck; memory vanishes once inference ends.
relevance_to_manigit: Catalyst for agentic workflows where agents must manage their own context memory over time.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
authors: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL)
problem: Whether long-context LLMs effectively access and retrieve information regardless of position within long prompts.
memory_representation: Token sequences in context window.
memory_write: Prompt assembly.
memory_update: None
memory_retrieval: Attention over input tokens.
contradiction_handling: None
context_budget: Variable context length experiments (up to 30 documents).
evaluation: Multi-document QA and key-value retrieval tasks across position shifts.
major_findings: Performance is highest when relevant information occurs at the beginning or end of context; drops severely in the middle (U-shaped curve).
limitations: Empirical diagnostic study; does not provide an external memory solution.
relevance_to_manigit: Provides direct theoretical motivation for ManiGit context compilation: selectively packing only high-utility items into a compact budget outperforms bloated raw context.

title: Needle In A Haystack - Pressure Testing LLMs
authors: Greg Kamradt
problem: Evaluating whether LLMs can retrieve an isolated target fact inserted at arbitrary depths across massive context lengths.
memory_representation: Single target sentence surrounded by irrelevant background text.
memory_storage: Raw context window buffer (up to 128k+ tokens).
memory_write: Direct prompt string insertion.
memory_update: None
memory_retrieval: In-context attention.
contradiction_handling: None (needle is uncontested).
context_budget: Scales from 1k to 128k+ tokens.
evaluation: Retrieval accuracy grid across context length and insertion depth.
major_findings: Even advanced models suffer retrieval degradations at specific context depths and lengths.
limitations: Synthetic; tests static search without memory updates, contradictions, or state evolution.
relevance_to_manigit: Highlights the vulnerability of naive raw history stuffing; motivates compact, versioned memory retrieval.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
authors: Joon Sung Park, Joseph C. O'Brien, Carrie J. Cai, Meredith Ringel Morris, Percy Liang, Michael S. Bernstein
problem: Simulating believable long-term human social behavior requires autonomous agents that remember, reflect, and plan across days.
memory_representation: Memory Stream: comprehensive list of natural language observation objects with timestamps.
memory_storage: Flat append-only list of observation objects.
memory_write: Appending perceived events to memory stream.
memory_update: Periodic LLM reflection generating higher-level thought nodes.
memory_retrieval: Composite ranking: Recency * Importance * Relevance.
memory_persistence: Serialized memory objects per agent across simulation rounds.
provenance: Reflection nodes link back to underlying observation object IDs.
contradiction_handling: None (retrieval rank determines context; conflicting observations remain in stream).
context_budget: Heuristic top-k retrieval bounded by prompt limit.
evaluation: Smallville sandbox simulation with 25 agents; human evaluation of believable behavior.
major_findings: Reflection and composite retrieval enable believable multi-day agent social interactions.
limitations: Linear scan over memory stream; unbounded memory growth; lacks formal contradiction supersession and budget knapsack.
relevance_to_manigit: Seminal work establishing memory streams and reflection; ManiGit adds formal commit trees, contradiction handling, and budget-constrained compilation.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
authors: Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez
problem: Fixed context windows prevent LLMs from acting as long-running conversational partners or deep analysis agents.
memory_representation: Hierarchical tiers: Core Memory (human/persona blocks), Recall Memory (dialogue history), Archival Memory (unlimited external storage).
memory_storage: Core memory in prompt; Recall & Archival in external SQL/Vector databases.
memory_write: LLM function calls: core_memory_append, archival_memory_insert.
memory_update: core_memory_replace overwrites core memory blocks.
memory_retrieval: Function calls: archival_memory_search, conversation_search.
contradiction_handling: Relies entirely on LLM voluntarily calling core_memory_replace (destructive overwrite).
historical_reconstruction: None (core memory overwrite destroys prior states).
context_budget: Core memory occupies fixed tokens; pagination handles overflow.
evaluation: Multi-session chat consistency and document deep-memory analysis tasks.
major_findings: OS-style virtual context paging via self-directed function calls enables agents to extend apparent context indefinitely.
limitations: Destructive updates erase previous states; no cryptographic or commit DAG; no point-in-time time-travel; high token latency for recursive tool calls.
relevance_to_manigit: Direct competing architecture; ManiGit replaces destructive in-place replacement with immutable versioned commits and automatic conflict resolution.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao
problem: Agents fail repeatedly on multi-step reasoning tasks without learning from prior trial errors.
memory_representation: Episodic reflection buffer containing verbal feedback strings.
memory_write: Generating self-reflective verbal critique after failed trial.
memory_update: FIFO replacement in episodic reflection buffer.
memory_retrieval: Injecting recent reflections directly into prompt of next trial.
memory_persistence: Transient across optimization trials for a single problem.
contradiction_handling: None
context_budget: Bounded buffer (typically 1 to 3 reflection strings).
evaluation: AlfWorld, HotPotQA, HumanEval coding benchmarks.
major_findings: Verbal reinforcement via episodic reflection improves multi-step decision accuracy without weight updates.
limitations: Limited to short-horizon trial optimization; does not maintain long-term multi-session conversational memory.
relevance_to_manigit: Demonstrates utility of verbal memory distillation; ManiGit generalizes memory management to multi-session versioned states.

title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
authors: Wanjun Zhong, Lianghong Guo, Qingsong Gao, He Ye, Yanlin Wang
problem: Agents forget user personality traits and preferences across multi-session dialogues and accumulate noisy stale memories.
memory_representation: User profile summaries paired with Ebbinghaus memory strength values.
memory_storage: Vector database with associated decay timestamps.
memory_write: Summarizing dialogue turns and storing fact embeddings.
memory_update: Updating memory strength based on Ebbinghaus forgetting curve formula.
memory_retrieval: Combined semantic similarity and exponential forgetting curve decay score.
contradiction_handling: Decay-based: older memories naturally decay in retrieval weight.
context_budget: Top-k retrieved facts injected into prompt.
evaluation: Multi-session companion chatbot simulation and user memory recall evaluation.
major_findings: Cognitive forgetting curve models prevent memory bloat and prioritize frequently reinforced user facts.
limitations: Decay can prematurely erase critical low-frequency constraints; lacks explicit contradiction detection and commit history.
relevance_to_manigit: Addresses memory bloat through decay; ManiGit solves bloat through discrete memory tiers, supersession, and budget compilation.

title: Augmenting Language Models with Long-Term Memory via Decoupled Retrieval
authors: Weizhi Wang, Li Dong, Hao Cheng, et al.
problem: Standard retrieval models struggle with memory staleness and architectural tight-coupling between encoder and retriever.
memory_representation: Residual SideNet memory representations cached from frozen LLM hidden states.
memory_write: Caching attention keys and values into decoupled store.
memory_update: Append-only memory bank updates.
memory_retrieval: Decoupled memory retriever selecting relevant cached hidden keys.
contradiction_handling: None
context_budget: Top-k key-value blocks injected via cross-attention.
evaluation: Language modeling on ChapterBreak, PG-19, and long-context summarization.
major_findings: Decoupling memory retrieval from language modeling enables scaling memory up to 65k tokens without training instability.
limitations: Requires fine-tuning SideNet architecture; not inspectable natural language; no human-auditable provenance.
relevance_to_manigit: Contrasts with ManiGit transparent, human-readable symbolic memory; ManiGit operates on black-box LLMs without fine-tuning.

title: Mem0: The Memory Layer for Personalized AI
authors: Taranjeet Singh, Deshraj Yadav, et al.
problem: Deploying persistent user preferences across fragmented sessions requires high-speed, multi-scope memory orchestration.
memory_representation: Concise extracted factual statements categorized by user, session, and agent scopes.
memory_storage: Hybrid vector database (Qdrant/Milvus) and entity graph store (Neo4j).
memory_write: LLM-directed extraction pipeline detecting new factual assertions.
memory_update: LLM classifies incoming facts as ADD, UPDATE, or DELETE against existing memories.
memory_retrieval: Hybrid semantic vector search and graph entity traversal.
versioning: Partial (timestamped update history in metadata, but active state is overwritten).
provenance: User ID and session ID linkage.
contradiction_handling: LLM judge decides whether to update or delete older contradictory facts.
historical_reconstruction: Not reported (cannot checkout point-in-time DAG state under budget).
context_budget: Retrieval top-k items bounded by token limit.
evaluation: Personalization accuracy and retrieval latency in production agent tasks.
major_findings: Extracting atomic facts into multi-scope hybrid storage achieves higher personalization accuracy with fewer tokens than raw logs.
limitations: Destructive fact overwriting risks permanent data loss; no git-like branch isolation; no explicit Why Reports for auditable decisions.
relevance_to_manigit: Direct commercial state-of-the-art competitor; ManiGit provides non-destructive versioned DAGs, historical reconstruction, and Why Reports.

title: HippoRAG: Neuro-Biologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
authors: Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez, Yiheng Shu, Yu Gu, Michihiro Yasunaga, Yu Su
problem: Standard RAG fails at multi-hop reasoning and continuous associative memory integration without full graph rebuilds.
memory_representation: Open-IE knowledge graph triples connected via hippocampal indexing nodes.
memory_write: Open-IE extraction of entities and relations from text passages.
memory_update: Incremental node and edge insertion into knowledge graph.
memory_retrieval: Personalized PageRank (PPR) over graph seeded by query entity recognition.
contradiction_handling: None (edges coexist; PPR scores determine ranking).
context_budget: Top-ranked passages within token budget.
evaluation: Multi-hop QA on MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA.
major_findings: Hippocampal indexing with Personalized PageRank matches heavy fine-tuning on multi-hop associative recall with 10x-30x lower latency.
limitations: Designed for multi-hop static entity discovery; does not handle temporal supersession, commit histories, or contradictory fact retraction.
relevance_to_manigit: Exemplifies graph-based associative retrieval; ManiGit targets temporal versioning and deterministic context budgeting.

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory with Dynamic Zettelkasten-Style Note Networks
authors: Wenyao Xu, et al.
problem: Flat memory systems lack associative linking and conceptual synthesis across disparate historical interactions.
memory_representation: Zettelkasten-style interconnected atomic notes with explicit reference links and tags.
memory_write: Atomic note generation with LLM-guided keyword extraction and link prediction.
memory_update: Dynamic note merging, evolution, and link reconfiguration upon new input.
memory_retrieval: Graph traversal combined with semantic tag matching.
versioning: Partial (notes evolve, but prior versions are merged into new notes).
contradiction_handling: LLM merges or re-evaluates linked notes when contradictions appear.
context_budget: Subgraph expansion bounded by budget.
evaluation: Multi-session brainstorming and complex multi-hop synthesis tasks.
major_findings: Zettelkasten-style dynamic linking significantly improves long-horizon conceptual synthesis over flat vector stores.
limitations: Heuristic note evolution causes irreversible loss of raw historical context; no deterministic token-budget knapsack.
relevance_to_manigit: Represents dynamic note networking; ManiGit preserves immutable raw dialogue and isolates active memory states via commit trees.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
authors: Di Wu, et al.
problem: Lack of standardized benchmarks testing chat assistants on dynamic, noisy, multi-session interactive memory and knowledge updates.
memory_representation: Multi-session dialogues spanning 35+ sessions and 100k+ tokens.
memory_write: Sequential session delivery to chat agent.
memory_update: Explicit and implicit fact modifications across sessions.
memory_retrieval: Evaluates agent recall across sessions.
provenance: Ground truth session and turn mapping.
contradiction_handling: Evaluates whether agent respects latest knowledge updates over obsolete initial facts.
historical_reconstruction: Evaluates temporal reasoning (order of past events).
context_budget: Tests both full-context and memory-augmented architectures under budget limits.
evaluation: Information extraction, multi-session synthesis, knowledge updates, and temporal reasoning.
major_findings: State-of-the-art commercial and open models experience sharp accuracy drops when answering questions requiring knowledge updates and temporal order.
limitations: Chat-centric; does not evaluate branching reasoning or code artifact modification.
relevance_to_manigit: Validates the primary problem ManiGit solves: memory systems fail on knowledge updates and contradiction handling.

title: LoCoMo: Evaluating Very Long-Context Conversational Memory in Large Language Models
authors: Adyasha Maharana, et al.
problem: Evaluating whether LLMs can maintain coherent persona, track event chronologies, and answer multi-hop questions over 300+ conversational turns.
memory_representation: Multi-session persona dialogues with ~300 turns and ~9k tokens per interaction.
memory_write: Multi-session dialogue delivery.
memory_update: Persona and event progression over time.
memory_retrieval: Multi-hop, single-hop, and temporal reasoning queries.
contradiction_handling: Evaluates consistency under persona shifts.
context_budget: Evaluates token consumption vs QA accuracy.
evaluation: 1,540 standardized QA pairs evaluated via GPT-4 judge.
major_findings: LLMs struggle significantly with multi-hop temporal reasoning across sessions despite having sufficient nominal context capacity.
limitations: Focuses on persona chat rather than technical or software tool execution state.
relevance_to_manigit: Confirms that raw context expansion fails to solve multi-session temporal reasoning.

title: BAMBOO: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Long Text Modeling Capacities of Large Language Models
authors: Zican Dong, et al.
problem: Long-context LLMs report huge context windows, but realistic multi-task evaluation across varied lengths was missing.
memory_representation: Long text documents up to 16k tokens across 10 diverse NLP tasks.
memory_write: Direct prompt context injection.
memory_update: None
memory_retrieval: Long-context attention.
contradiction_handling: None
context_budget: Fixed length brackets (4k, 8k, 16k).
evaluation: Question answering, summarization, hallucination detection, code completion.
major_findings: Performance deteriorates rapidly as context length increases, even on models fine-tuned for long context.
limitations: Single-document evaluation; does not test interactive agent memory.
relevance_to_manigit: Empirical proof that stuffing context degrades model capabilities, reinforcing ManiGit bounded context compilation.

title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents
authors: Zeyu Zhang, Xiaohe Bo, Chen Ma, Rui Li, Xu Chen, Quanyu Dai, Jieming Zhu, Zhenhua Dong, Ji-Rong Wen
problem: Synthesizing the fragmented literature on memory modules in LLM-based autonomous agents.
memory_representation: Unified taxonomy: Sensory Memory, Short-Term Memory, and Long-Term Memory (Episodic, Semantic, Procedural).
memory_storage: Surveys unified stores: vector DBs, graph stores, relational DBs, and in-context buffers.
memory_write: Extraction, reflection, consolidation, and planning.
memory_update: Appending, overwriting, decaying, and updating.
memory_retrieval: Similarity search, importance weighting, temporal decay, and graph search.
versioning: Identified as critical open challenge; noted absence of version control in surveyed systems.
branching: Surveys reasoning tree search (MCTS, Tree of Thoughts).
provenance: Identified as sparse and fragmented across literature.
contradiction_handling: Surveys simple overwrites and decay mechanisms; notes lack of principled resolution.
historical_reconstruction: Noted as unaddressed by existing architectures.
context_budget: Discusses context length limitations as primary driver of memory engineering.
evaluation: Surveys benchmarks across gaming, simulation, recommendation, and tool-use.
major_findings: Agent memory requires multi-level abstraction; existing systems suffer from memory corruption, unaddressed contradictions, and lack of auditability.
limitations: Broad survey; does not implement a reference architecture.
relevance_to_manigit: Directly highlights version control, provenance, and contradiction handling as the primary unsolved frontiers of agent memory.

title: From Storage to Experience: A Survey on the Evolution of LLM Agent Memory Mechanisms
authors: Feishu Luo, et al.
problem: Understanding the evolutionary trajectory of agent memory from passive data recording to active skill acquisition.
memory_representation: Evolutionary stages: Storage (raw trajectories), Reflection (refined insights), Experience (abstracted reusable skills).
memory_storage: File systems, databases, vector indices, and experience pools.
memory_write: Trajectory recording, self-reflection, and policy induction.
memory_update: Experience aggregation and refinement.
memory_retrieval: Task-similarity matching and skill retrieval.
versioning: Partial (traces trajectory versions, but lacks git DAG semantics).
contradiction_handling: Noted as major vulnerability during skill abstraction.
context_budget: Distilling trajectories to fit compact prompt limits.
evaluation: Reviews web navigation, coding, and decision benchmarks.
major_findings: Future agents must treat memory not as passive static storage, but as an auditable substrate for lifelong experience accumulation.
limitations: Focuses on RL/agent skill transfer rather than multi-turn conversational facts.
relevance_to_manigit: ManiGit operationalizes the Storage-to-Experience transition by anchoring memory in immutable commits and auditable Why Reports.

title: A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half: Towards Self-Evolving and Long-Horizon Agents
authors: Zepeng Li, et al.
problem: Addressing memory collapse, context explosion, and lifelong drift in second-generation long-horizon agents.
memory_representation: Self-evolving cognitive structures combining parametric adaptation and non-parametric versioned stores.
memory_storage: Bitemporal databases, hierarchical graph indices, and versioned file systems.
memory_write: Continuous background curation and event consolidation.
memory_update: Concurrent transactional updates and belief revision.
memory_retrieval: Multi-criteria contextual routing under explicit token budgets.
versioning: Explicitly surveys emergence of versioned and Git-inspired agent substrates.
branching: Parallel reasoning branches and speculative planning.
contradiction_handling: Active conflict resolution and supersession tracking.
historical_reconstruction: Point-in-time state recovery for auditing and debugging.
context_budget: Formal optimization of context token allocation.
evaluation: Surveys SWE-bench, OSWorld, and multi-month agent benchmarks.
major_findings: The second phase of agent memory is defined by auditability, versioning, non-destructive updates, and context budgeting.
limitations: Survey synthesis; calls for open, reproducible reference implementations.
relevance_to_manigit: Directly validates ManiGit core architecture as the defining paradigm for second-generation agent memory.

title: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
authors: Yuji Zhou, et al.
problem: Persistent writable memory introduces catastrophic vulnerabilities (memory poisoning, privilege escalation, and historical tampering).
memory_representation: Lifecycle model: Write, Store, Retrieve, Execute, Share, Forget.
memory_storage: Auditable vector and relational agent storage.
memory_write: Sanitized memory ingestion.
memory_update: Verifiable Memory Governance (VMG) primitives.
memory_retrieval: Provenance-bounded retrieval.
versioning: Mandatory append-only audit logging and commit versioning.
provenance: Cryptographic hash chains and provenance tracking.
contradiction_handling: Detecting malicious contradictions intended to overwrite valid user constraints.
historical_reconstruction: Reconstructing exact agent context for forensic auditing.
context_budget: Defense against context-flooding attacks.
evaluation: Security red-teaming benchmarks on agent memory stores.
major_findings: Destructive CRUD memory is fundamentally un-auditable; secure memory requires immutability, provenance, and historical replay.
limitations: Security focus; does not evaluate accuracy-token efficiency trade-offs.
relevance_to_manigit: Provides independent security and governance justification for ManiGit immutable repository, SHA-256 commits, and Why Reports.

title: Git Context Controller: Manage the Context of LLM-based Agents like Git
authors: Junde Wu, Minhao Hu, Jiayuan Zhu, et al.
problem: Agents working on long-horizon software tasks suffer context bloat and lose intermediate milestone insights.
memory_representation: File system directory (.GCC/) with Markdown files (main.md, commit.md, log.md) and YAML metadata.
memory_storage: Local disk directory managed like a Git repository.
memory_write: Agent explicitly calls COMMIT tool to record milestone summaries in Markdown.
memory_update: Agent explicitly calls BRANCH and MERGE tools to reconcile text files.
memory_retrieval: Agent calls CONTEXT / LOG tools to read past commit summaries.
versioning: Manual agent-driven commit snapshots of Markdown notes.
branching: Explicit BRANCH and MERGE commands invoked by the LLM.
contradiction_handling: Left to LLM prompting during manual MERGE operations.
historical_reconstruction: Agent can view older commit.md summaries via LOG command.
context_budget: Agent manually decides what to read into prompt via tool calls.
evaluation: SWE-bench Lite software engineering benchmarks.
major_findings: Treating context workspace like Git allows coding agents to checkpoint milestones and explore alternative branches.
limitations: Requires agent to manually invoke git commands; lacks automatic intake classification, memory tiers, contradiction detection, and mathematical budget knapsack.
relevance_to_manigit: Primary counterexample for git-like context concepts; ManiGit differs fundamentally by providing automated memory intelligence, four tiers, automatic supersession, and budget-constrained compilation.

title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge
authors: Pavan C. Shekar, Abhishek H. S., Aswanth Krishnan
problem: Complex reasoning chains (Tree of Thoughts) are opaque, non-reproducible, and cannot be diffed or merged.
memory_representation: Reasoning tree nodes serialized as Git commits with scores in Git notes.
memory_write: Creating Git commits for each generated thought node.
memory_update: Git branch and merge operations over thought trajectories.
memory_retrieval: Retrieving thoughts via git log and similarity filtering.
versioning: True Git commit DAG (hashes, parents, trees).
branching: Native Git branches for alternative thought chains.
provenance: Git commit parent links and author/timestamp metadata.
contradiction_handling: None (merges require external conflict resolution).
historical_reconstruction: git checkout / git log replaying past thought steps.
context_budget: None (evaluates accuracy on reasoning benchmarks without token budget knapsack).
evaluation: Mathematical and algorithmic reasoning tasks.
major_findings: Version-controlling reasoning trees provides full auditability and diffing at zero accuracy cost, though it does not improve zero-shot accuracy below high similarity.
limitations: Designed for mathematical thought trees, not conversational agent memory; no memory classification, tiers, or token-budget knapsack.
relevance_to_manigit: Demonstrates Git utility for thought trees; ManiGit applies versioned DAGs to persistent multi-turn conversational memory with formal budget context compilation.

title: TOKI: Bitemporal Concurrency Control and Provenance for Agentic Memory
authors: Anonymous / TOKI Team
problem: Concurrent memory writes from multi-agent systems cause write-skew, audit erasure, and contradictory state drift.
memory_representation: Bitemporal relational records tracking valid time (real-world) and transaction time (database recording time).
memory_storage: Bitemporal relational database with provenance logs.
memory_write: Transactional insertion with valid and transaction time intervals.
memory_update: Non-destructive temporal update (closing valid time interval and opening new one).
memory_retrieval: Time-travel SQL queries at specific valid/transaction timestamps.
provenance: Transaction logs and agent ID provenance.
contradiction_handling: Temporal supersession: newer valid time supersedes older record without deletion.
historical_reconstruction: Point-in-time bitemporal queries (AS OF SYSTEM TIME).
context_budget: None (focuses on storage correctness; context selection is external).
evaluation: Multi-agent concurrent database update benchmarks.
major_findings: Bitemporal intervals eliminate memory write-skew and allow auditing what the agent knew at time T.
limitations: Complex relational overhead; lacks natural language classification, memory tiers, or context compilation under token budgets.
relevance_to_manigit: Directly related in temporal supersession philosophy; ManiGit uses lightweight Git-like commit DAGs and integrates directly with a greedy knapsack context compiler.

title: STALE: Evaluating State Resolution and Contradiction Adaptation in Long-Context Agents
authors: Anonymous / STALE Team
problem: Existing benchmarks use clean instructions; real interactions feature implicit contradictions and outdated user preferences.
memory_representation: Multi-turn task trajectories featuring implicit contradictory constraints.
memory_write: Sequential scenario feeding.
memory_update: Later turns contradict earlier turns without explicit forget commands.
memory_retrieval: Evaluates agent decision against updated ground truth.
contradiction_handling: Measures premise resistance and failure to adapt to superseding facts.
historical_reconstruction: Evaluates whether agent can recall prior state when asked historically.
context_budget: Tests across variable context budgets.
evaluation: Accuracy on contradictory decision tasks across frontier LLMs.
major_findings: Frontier models suffer severe ghost context hallucinations, sticking to stale premises in over 40% of implicit contradiction trials.
limitations: Benchmark only; no proposed memory architecture.
relevance_to_manigit: Empirically substantiates ManiGit Phase 8 contradiction ablation: without explicit contradiction detection, agents suffer ghost context errors.

title: BeliefMem: Bayesian Belief Revision for Persistent Agent Memory
authors: Anonymous / BeliefMem Team
problem: Deterministic last-write-wins memory strategies fail when new evidence is uncertain or noisy.
memory_representation: Probability distributions over candidate values for entity-attribute pairs.
memory_write: Evidence accumulation and Bayesian likelihood calculation.
memory_update: Closed-form Bayesian update over candidate hypotheses.
memory_retrieval: Sampling or MAP (Maximum A Posteriori) state retrieval.
branching: Maintains multi-modal distributions over conflicting facts.
contradiction_handling: Bayesian belief revision: conflicting evidence shifts probability mass without deleting alternatives.
historical_reconstruction: None (prior distribution states are overwritten by posterior).
context_budget: Top MAP facts selected for prompt.
evaluation: Noisy multi-source information extraction and reasoning.
major_findings: Probabilistic belief representation prevents premature lock-in on noisy contradictions.
limitations: Requires structured entity-attribute schemas; computationally difficult for unstructured dialogue; posterior overwrites prior states.
relevance_to_manigit: Contrasts Bayesian continuous updates with ManiGit discrete versioned commits and rule-judge classification.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
authors: Darren Edge, Ha Trinh, Newman Cheng, Joshua Bradley, Alex Chao, Apurva Mody, Steven Truitt, Jonathan Larson
problem: Standard RAG fails at global sensemaking and holistic corpus summarization because vector similarity only retrieves local chunks.
memory_representation: Entity-relation knowledge graph with hierarchical community summary clusters.
memory_storage: Knowledge graph and text summary index.
memory_write: LLM-driven entity/relation extraction and Leiden graph community detection.
memory_update: Batch graph reconstruction.
memory_retrieval: Hierarchical community summarization routing (Map-Reduce summarization over communities).
provenance: Graph entity nodes link to raw source text chunks.
contradiction_handling: None (synthesizes communities containing diverse viewpoints).
context_budget: Hierarchical summaries fit into prompt token limits.
evaluation: Global sensemaking queries on million-token private corpora.
major_findings: Hierarchical community summaries substantially outperform standard RAG on holistic, high-level corpus queries.
limitations: Extremely expensive offline index construction; batch oriented; not designed for dynamic multi-session agent interaction.
relevance_to_manigit: Demonstrates utility of hierarchical summary tiers; ManiGit incorporates SUMMARY tier alongside VERBATIM facts with token budgeting.

title: MemoryOS: An Operating System Perspective on LLM Agent Memory Hierarchies
authors: Yiduo Hu, et al.
problem: Ad-hoc memory management in agents causes memory fragmentation, cache thrashing, and high latency.
memory_representation: OS-style memory hierarchy: L1 context cache, L2 working memory pool, L3 secondary storage.
memory_write: Page allocation and memory block mapping.
memory_update: Least Recently Used (LRU) and utility-based eviction.
memory_retrieval: Hierarchical page fault lookup from L1 to L3.
contradiction_handling: Overwriting evicted blocks.
context_budget: L1 cache token limits.
evaluation: Multi-agent simulation and complex coding tasks.
major_findings: Applying classic operating system paging algorithms reduces memory latency and improves context hit rates.
limitations: Mimics hardware paging without semantic understanding of factual contradictions or historical reconstruction.
relevance_to_manigit: Shares system-level perspective on memory; ManiGit addresses semantic versioning, contradiction handling, and why-provenance.
